title: Protocol and Service Weak-Configuration Attacks
description: Common breakthrough points for non-HTTP services
detail:
FTP 21: anonymous login; configuration file path exposure; vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor
SSH 22: weak credentials; user enumeration (differences in password prompts); older OpenSSH username enumeration CVE-2018-15473
SMB 445: anonymous IPC$ enumeration (enum4linux/crackmapexec --shares); EternalBlue (older internal hosts); signing disabled → relay
SMTP 25: user enumeration (VRFY/EXPN); open relay
POP3/IMAP: credential reuse
Redis 6379: unauthenticated (write crontab/SSH key/web shell/master-slave RCE)
MySQL 3306: weak credentials → UDF/write files; client-read chain
MSSQL 1433: weak sa credentials → xp_cmdshell
RDP 3389: weak credentials; BlueKeep (older systems)
MongoDB/Elasticsearch/Memcached: unauthenticated (11211 Memcached can be abused for DDoS, but do not touch that surface)
Zookeeper 2181/Jenkins/Kubernetes: see the corresponding entries
Approach: run nmap -sV across all ports first, then check each service against the list.
